question: Incisional biopsy of a parotid mass is contraindicated because it risks tumour cell seeding along the biopsy tract and increases the risk of facial nerve injury, making fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) the appropriate initial tissue diagnostic procedure.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. This statement is true. Incisional biopsy of parotid masses is specifically contraindicated for the reasons stated. FNAC guided by ultrasound is the recommended first-line tissue sampling technique before planning surgery.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Incisional biopsy of a parotid mass breaches the tumour capsule, risks implantation metastasis, and endangers the facial nerve. FNAC is the safe, recommended tissue diagnosis method. Superficial parotidectomy with facial nerve preservation is the definitive diagnostic and therapeutic procedure when indicated.
